title: Lands’ End, Post Sears, Replaces Its Chief (Published 2015)
summary: Lands' End announced it is replacing its chief executive with Federica Marchionni, president of Dolce & Gabbana, signaling a new direction for the brand after its separation from Sears Holding Corporation. Marchionni aims to expand Lands' End into new markets and channels while retaining its core values. The outgoing CEO, Edgar Huber, stated he accomplished his goals following the successful spin-off.

title: Supermicro X10DAX (Intel C612) Workstation Motherboard Review
summary: This review examines the Supermicro X10DAX workstation motherboard, highlighting its Hyper-Speed overclocking features and support for multi-GPU configurations. The article details its specifications, layout, BIOS, and performance through various benchmarks, comparing it to the X10DAi model. It concludes that the X10DAX offers excellent performance and stability for enthusiasts and professional applications requiring high-end computing power.

title: TurboTax Resumes State Tax Filing Service Nationwide After Fraud Concerns
summary: TurboTax resumed its state tax filing services nationwide after temporarily pausing them due to fraud concerns. Intuit, the maker of TurboTax, stated that the fraud instances did not result from a security breach of its systems and that they are working with states and security expert Palantir. This suspension followed actions by states like Minnesota, Utah, and Alabama to halt processing returns submitted through third-party software due to suspicious activity.

title: FAA shoots down Amazon's drone delivery plans
summary: Amazon expressed disappointment after the FAA's proposed drone rules made their drone delivery program, Prime Air, unviable in the US. The rules require drones to fly within the operator's line of sight and not over people, which Amazon and other industry groups argue defeats the purpose of commercial drone delivery. While other countries are moving forward with commercial drone use, the US faces significant regulatory hurdles.

title: Q&A: Carlos López Blanco, Telefónica’s head of public and regulatory affairs
summary: Carlos López Blanco, Telefónica’s head of public and regulatory affairs, discusses his career trajectory and the evolving challenges faced by the telecommunications industry, particularly in the shift towards a digital economy. He emphasizes Telefónica's focus on customer-centric policies and the need for consistent regulation across all digital services, including "over-the-top" players. Blanco also highlights the company's digital manifesto, advocating for an open and safe internet, fair competition, and transparency from all market participants.

title: Amazon, Flipkart fuel DHL's e-tail expansion
summary: Blue Dart Express Ltd, a unit of DHL Express, is significantly expanding its operations in India due to the booming e-commerce market fueled by companies like Amazon and Flipkart. The company is adding a Boeing Co 757 freighter to its fleet and building warehouses to support online sellers. This expansion addresses the immense demand in India's rapidly growing e-commerce sector, which is projected to reach 3 percent of the entire Indian retail market by 2020.

title: How ‘House of Cards’ Drove Netflix’s Colossal Growth
summary: The article discusses how Netflix's original series "House of Cards" was a turning point for the company, transforming it into a major player in television content. The show, launched in 2013, was a critical and financial success, leading to significant subscriber growth and a tripling of Netflix's stock price. Despite its success, Netflix faces the challenge of consistently delivering high-quality original programming to retain its subscriber base.

title: Why House of Cards marks a turning point in TV history
summary: House of Cards is highlighted as a pivotal series that transformed Netflix into an internet powerhouse and redefined television. The show's success justified Netflix's significant investment in original programming, leading its stock to nearly triple and increasing its subscriber base to 57 million. Its influence also prompted other online services to invest heavily in their own original content, marking a significant turning point in the industry.
